questions.text: Why are the Kailasa Temple at Ellora and the Elephanta Caves famous?
questions.text_as_printed: Why are the Kailasa Temple at Ellora and the Elephanta Caves famous? (Average)

answer.value:
The Kailasanatha Temple at Ellora and the Elephanta Caves, built during the Rashtrakuta period, are among the greatest masterpieces of Indian sculpture and architecture. The main features that made them famous are as follows:
Kailasanatha Temple, Ellora (Maharashtra): It is located in Sambhajinagar (Aurangabad) district of Maharashtra. It was carved by the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I.
Monolithic wonder: It is the largest rock-cut architectural monument in the world. Without using any bricks, sand, or cement, the entire temple was carved out of a single massive hill rock.
Elephanta Caves (Maharashtra): It is located on a small island in the Arabian Sea near Mumbai (its original name is Gharapuri). This cave temple was built during the Rashtrakuta period.
The magnificent Trimurti Shiva sculpture: The main attraction of this cave is the approximately 20-foot-high Trimurti Shiva (Sadashiva) sculpture, in which the three forms of Shiva (Creator, Preserver, and Destroyer) are carved with exceptional artistic skill. It is regarded as one of the world's finest works of sculpture.

questions.text: Explain the military achievements of Govinda III.
questions.text_as_printed: Explain the military achievements of Govinda III. (Average)

answer.value:
Military achievements of Govinda III
Among the kings of the Rashtrakuta dynasty, Govinda III (A.D. 793-814) was the most valiant and greatest emperor. During his reign the fame of the Rashtrakutas spread from the Himalayas in the north to Kanyakumari in the south. His major military achievements are as follows:
Suppression of internal rebellion (defeat of the confederacy).
Northern Indian campaign.
Conquest of Malwa and Gujarat.
Subjugation of the kings of South India: Chalukyas of Vengi; Gangas and Pallavas.
Surrender of the king of Sinhala (Sri Lanka).

questions.text: Which temple is called the "Emperor among the Temples"? Why?
questions.text_as_printed: Which temple is called the "Emperor among the Temples"? Why? (Difficult)

answer.value:
The Mahadeva Temple at Itagi, located in Yelburga Taluk of Koppal district, is called the "Emperor of Temples" (Devalaya Chakravarti). It was built in A.D. 1112 by Mahadeva Dandanayaka, the commander of the Kalyani Chalukya king Vikramaditya VI. Reasons:
Unparalleled architectural beauty: It is the grandest and most beautifully carved temple in the Kalyani Chalukya style; the intricate carvings on its walls, pillars, and towers are among the finest examples of sculpture in South India.
Reference in the inscription: In the contemporary inscription found within the temple premises, poets described it as the "Chakravarti of Temples" (the emperor of all temples).
Magnificent Mahamantapa: The temple has a spacious open Mahamantapa with 68 pillars; the carvings on each pillar and the Bhuvaneshwari ceiling design captivate visitors.

questions.text: Explain why the Brihadishwara Temple is famous.
questions.text_as_printed: Explain why the Brihadishwara Temple is famous. (Difficult)

answer.value:
The Brihadisvara Temple (Rajarajesvara Temple) at Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu, is one of the grandest and most historic temples in India. It is famous for several reasons:
Architectural marvel: An outstanding example of Dravidian architecture, built entirely of granite; thousands of tons of stone were brought from elsewhere to construct this massive structure.
The tall "Vimana" (Tower): The main tower is about 216 feet high, one of the tallest temple towers in the world; the Kumbha at the top is carved from a single stone weighing around 80 tons.
The mystery of the shadow: By a once-popular belief, the shadow of the main tower does not fall on the ground at noon, regarded as evidence of its architectural precision.
The magnificent Nandi statue: A huge Nandi carved from a single stone stands at the entrance, about 13 feet high and 16 feet long, one of the largest in India.
Chola history and UNESCO recognition: Built in A.D. 1010 by Rajaraja Chola I; included in the UNESCO World Heritage Sites list; the walls carry beautiful sculptures and some of the oldest Chola-period frescoes.
